questions.q: Why does the CI workflow run dbt against a dedicated CI schema instead of prod?
options: There is no real reason -- it's an arbitrary convention
The CI schema is faster to query than prod
So a bad model in a pull request can fail its tests without ever touching the data leadership's dashboard actually reads from
Snowflake does not allow dbt to connect to a production schema from GitHub Actions
questions.explain: Isolating CI runs from prod is the actual protection CI/CD provides here -- without it, untested PR code would run against the real production marts.

options: Selects models randomly for faster CI runs
Runs only models that changed in this PR, plus everything downstream of them -- not the entire project every time
Runs the entire dbt project regardless of what changed
Only runs tests, never models
questions.explain: This is Slim CI's core mechanism -- scoping the CI run to what actually changed (plus downstream dependents) rather than re-testing everything on every PR.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Slim CI matters beyond just raw speed, as the project grows?
options: Without Slim CI, dbt would produce incorrect test results
Slim CI is required by GitHub Actions for any dbt project with more than 10 models
A CI run that re-tests everything gets slower as the project grows until people start skipping it; a scoped run stays fast regardless of project size
Slim CI only matters for very small projects, not growing ones
questions.explain: The real risk of an unscoped CI run isn't just slowness today -- it's that a team eventually starts ignoring or skipping a CI check that's become too slow to wait for.

questions.q: Why does this workflow use dbt build instead of separate dbt run and dbt test steps?
options: dbt run and dbt test cannot both be used in a GitHub Actions workflow
Separate steps would cause a syntax error in the YAML file
dbt build runs models and tests together in dependency order as one pass/fail signal, which is all CI needs per PR
dbt build is faster because it skips running tests entirely
questions.explain: CI only needs one combined pass/fail result per PR -- dbt build provides that directly, matching the git-cicd course's own CI pattern.

questions.q: What triggers this GitHub Actions workflow to run?
options: A nightly scheduled cron trigger, unrelated to pull requests
A manual button click in the GitHub UI only
A pull request that touches files under dbt/driftwood_analytics/
Any push to any branch in the entire repository, regardless of what changed
questions.explain: The workflow's `on: pull_request` with a `paths` filter scopes it specifically to PRs touching the dbt project's files.
